agent_supports: yes (2 of the row's 4 triggers present in aider 0.86.2 — first-use workspace/provider trust prompts at main.py:122/191 and onboarding.py:93, and a mid-turn product review at base_coder.py:1415 confirm_ask("Try to proceed anyway?") raised BEFORE any LLM call; sandbox and MCP triggers absent, cited as empty scans)
daemon_capability: incapable (the dialog's entry has no distinguishable trace — only unmarked status blockquotes on the shared tool_output channel — and its release has NO trace at all; all five waiting rules unreachable, and IdleFlush reports the blocked session as ready after 1500ms)

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: incapable
driver_capability: gap:permission-approval

## What the scenario requires

A blocking dialog attached to NO tool call: nothing carries the entry into
`waiting` and nothing carries the release back out. The row asserts both edges
plus a >=15s trailing idle that catches a session left pinned at `waiting`. It
is explicitly NOT `tool-gate-permission-prompt` and NOT
`permission-gate-non-mutating-tool`, where an open tool call carries both edges.

## agent_supports: yes — the four-trigger census

All four triggers the row lists were checked against the installed aider 0.86.2
package. Two are present, two are absent, and the absences are cited as empty
scans rather than asserted.

1. Sandbox or network-access confirmation — **ABSENT**. `grep -in sandbox`
   across every `.py` in the installed aider 0.86.2 package returns zero
   matches. Aider has no sandbox model and no network-egress gate. (Its one
   network-shaped prompt, `check_for_urls` -> "Add URL to the chat?"
   (coders/base_coder.py:976), is attached to a web-fetch read and therefore
   belongs to `permission-gate-non-mutating-tool`, not here — using it would be
   exactly the substitution this row forbids.)

2. First-use trust prompt for the workspace or a configured server — **PRESENT**,
   three of them, all startup-scoped:
   - `main.py:122` — `confirm_ask("No git repo found, create one to track
     aider's changes (recommended)?")`. A workspace trust prompt in the literal
     sense: aider will not manage the directory until the user answers.
   - `main.py:191` — `confirm_ask(f"Add {patterns} to .gitignore
     (recommended)?")`.
   - `onboarding.py:93` — `confirm_ask("Login to OpenRouter or create a free
     account?")`, the first-use provider trust/auth prompt.

3. Server-driven MCP elicitation — **ABSENT**. Every `.py` in the installed
   package was scanned for `mcp|MCP|modelcontextprotocol`: zero files matched,
   and `grep -in mcp args.py` is empty. aider 0.86.2 ships no MCP client, so no
   server can elicit anything.

4. Auto-mode or settings review the product raises before it proceeds —
   **PRESENT**, and unlike (2) these are mid-turn and elicitable by a `send`,
   which is what the row's process step 2 needs:
   - `Coder.check_tokens` (coders/base_coder.py:1396) ->
     `confirm_ask("Try to proceed anyway?")` at line 1415, raised when the
     estimated context exceeds the model's `max_input_tokens`. This is the
     cleanest instance of the row's shape in aider: it fires BEFORE the LLM
     call, so no tool call exists, none is in flight, and none can complete to
     release it. Purely a product-raised review.
   - `coders/base_coder.py:1604` `confirm_ask("Attempt to fix lint errors?")`
     and `:1620` `confirm_ask("Attempt to fix test errors?")`, raised after
     edits are applied — the lint/test run has already finished, so nothing is
     in flight when the dialog opens.
   - `utils.py:314` `confirm_ask("Run pip install?")` (self-upgrade) and
     `scrape.py:62` `confirm_ask("Install playwright?")`.

Two of four triggers present, with a mid-turn, prompt-elicitable instance among
them, is `agent_supports: yes` — the row says to use whichever trigger the agent
under test supports, and aider supports one squarely.

## daemon_capability: incapable

Same transport limit as the two sibling permission rows, and this row is where
it bites hardest, because there is not even a tool call to hang a heuristic on.

1. The transport. `Source` is `agent.FilesUnderCWD{Filename:
   ".aider.chat.history.md", Parser: agent.RawLineParser{...}}` (agent.go) —
   markdown chat history and nothing else. The adapter declares no hooks
   (`Permissions` carries only `ControlPermission` and the `history` observe
   permission; there is no `Hooks` field), so both hook-tier waiting signals
   are unreachable by construction.

2. What actually reaches the transcript around the dialog, stated precisely so
   this is not re-litigated. The question string is rendered ONLY via
   `prompt_session.prompt(question)` / `input(question)` (io.py:871-895) and is
   never written to the history file. What IS written is the preamble: for
   `check_tokens`, `io.tool_error(...)` at base_coder.py:1401 and the three
   `io.tool_output(...)` hint lines at 1402-1409 all reach
   `append_chat_history(..., blockquote=True)` (io.py:966-973 and 995-999), so
   the transcript gains
   `> Your estimated chat context of N tokens exceeds the M token limit for
   <model>!` and `> To reduce the chat context:` just before aider blocks.
   Those lines are indistinguishable from every other aider status line —
   `tool_output` is the same channel as the startup banner, `> Repo-map:` and
   all warnings — and they carry no marker that a dialog is open.
   `confirm_ask("Try to proceed anyway?")` passes no `subject`, no `group` and
   no `allow_never`, so on the answer NOTHING is written at all: the release
   edge has literally no trace.

3. The parser cannot emit a waiting-capable event. `ParseLineRaw` (parser.go)
   emits `user_message`, `assistant_message`, `tool_result` (Edit/Bash) and
   `turn_done` only, and drops non-error blockquotes with the comment "Other
   blockquote lines are aider status output (warnings, confirmation prompts,
   invocation echo). Ignore." The `> Your estimated chat context…` line does
   not match `errorRE` (`^>\s*\S*(?:Error|Exception)(?:[: ]|$)` — the first
   token is "Your"), so it is dropped as status output.

4. Every `waiting` rule is unreachable, and this row rules out the last one by
   its own definition. Of the five rules in `stateRules`
   (core/application/services/state_classifier.go:106-207):
   `SignalPermissionPrompt` and `SignalIdlePrompt` are hook-fed and aider has
   no hooks; `transcript_permission_prompt` needs
   `permission.requested`/`permission.completed` event kinds the aider parser
   never emits; `user_blocking_tool` needs an open tool named in
   `isUserBlockingToolName` (tailer_config.go:46-54) and aider only ever names
   "Edit" and "Bash"; and `SignalOpenToolStalled` — the transcript-tier
   fallback built precisely for "the agent is probably blocked on a permission
   prompt" — needs an OPEN tool call, which this row's premise excludes by
   definition and which aider's parser cannot produce anyway, since `toolCall()`
   emits `ToolUses` and `ToolResultIDs` in the SAME event so no tool is ever
   open across passes.

5. What a run would actually show is the failure the row's trailing idle exists
   to catch — but inverted. While `confirm_ask` blocks on stdin the transcript
   is quiet, so `Parser.IdleFlush` fires after `aiderIdleTurnDoneAfter` (1500ms,
   parser.go) and synthesizes a `turn_done`, which the classifier routes to
   **ready**. The row warns about a session left pinned at `waiting`; aider's
   failure is the opposite and arguably worse — a session pinned at a modal is
   reported as FINISHED, and every downstream consumer treats it as free.

`incapable`, not `bug`: the entry edge has no distinguishable trace (status
prose on a shared channel) and the release edge has no trace at all, so no
parser change could recover the arc from this transport. There is no signal the
daemon is given and mis-handles.

## driver_capability: gap:permission-approval

Same root cause as the sibling permission rows, and it applies to the tool-less
dialogs too because `io.yes` gates EVERY `confirm_ask` call, not just the
tool-attached ones.

1. `replaydata/agents/aider/driver-interactive.sh` hard-codes
   `AIDER_ARGS=( --no-auto-commits --yes-always --no-gitignore )`, and a
   recipe's `settings.aider_extra_args` can only APPEND. `--yes-always` cannot
   be negated: `args.py:760` declares it `action="store_true"`, not
   `argparse.BooleanOptionalAction` (which aider uses for ~30 other flags), so
   no `--no-yes-always` exists. With `io.yes is True`, `confirm_ask` returns
   immediately (io.py:869-870) and the dialog is never raised.
2. There is no step type to answer a dialog: `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash
   wait_turn interrupt sleep"`. The row's "the user answers the dialog
   (`keys`)" step has no implementation.
3. Two of this row's three startup triggers are additionally suppressed by the
   rig's own setup, independent of `--yes-always`: the driver git-inits
   `RUN_CWD` before launching aider (so `main.py:122`'s "No git repo found"
   branch is never reached) and passes `--no-gitignore` (so `main.py:191` is
   skipped). This is a rig property, not an aider property, and it is recorded
   here so a future run that observes no dialog does not misattribute the
   absence to the agent pillar.

## What would change this

Aider would have to write the dialog window into `.aider.chat.history.md` — an
open marker when `confirm_ask` is entered and a close when it returns — or ship
a hook channel the adapter could subscribe to. Neither exists in 0.86.2. A
daemon-side alternative would need an out-of-band signal that a watched process
is blocked on a terminal read, which neither this transport nor the current
classifier can express.
caveats: VACUOUS PASS: aider CAN reach `waiting`, but only via the trailing-question/cue text classifier (`turn ended with question or cue -> waiting`, core/application/services/state_classifier.go:437, over LastAssistantText). Because the dialog leaves no usable trace, ANY `waiting` a future aider recording of this cell shows is by construction NOT the dialog — and this row's premise (no tool call in flight) makes the confusion easier, not harder, since there is no open-tool evidence to cross-check against. Never accept a `waiting` episode as evidence for this row without naming which confirm_ask call produced it.

LOAD-BEARING ENVIRONMENT PROPERTIES that would make a run report "no dialog appeared" for a CONFIGURATION reason rather than an agent-capability one — check each before recording a negative: (a) driver-interactive.sh hard-codes --yes-always, which suppresses every confirm_ask; (b) the driver git-inits RUN_CWD, so main.py:122's "No git repo found" prompt is never reached; (c) the driver passes --no-gitignore, so main.py:191 is skipped; (d) analytics opt-in (main.py:649) fires only when analytics.need_to_ask is true, i.e. on a host that has not already answered it; (e) the OpenRouter onboarding prompt (onboarding.py:93) fires only when NO provider key is configured. Four of these are host or rig state, not aider behavior.

The mid-turn trigger this cell would use — confirm_ask("Try to proceed anyway?", coders/base_coder.py:1415, reached from check_tokens at 1396) — requires the estimated context to exceed the model's max_input_tokens. That figure comes from the model's litellm metadata, so eliciting it deterministically means pinning a small-context model or padding the chat with /read-only files; the recipe cannot assume any particular model's window.

NOT a silent transcript, and the difference matters for anyone re-litigating incapable-vs-bug: io.tool_error and io.tool_output both append blockquotes to .aider.chat.history.md (io.py:966-973, 995-999), so check_tokens' preamble (`> Your estimated chat context of N tokens exceeds…`) IS written just before aider blocks. It is still not a usable entry edge — it rides the same channel as every other status line and carries no dialog marker — and confirm_ask("Try to proceed anyway?") passes no subject/group/allow_never, so the ANSWER writes nothing at all and the release edge has no trace whatsoever.

daemon_capability is derived from source reading, not from a recording — no aider run of this cell exists, and none is possible under the current driver. The claim that the session is reported `ready` while the dialog is open follows from Parser.IdleFlush's 1500ms window firing over a quiet transcript; it is a provisional emission claim in the assess sense and would be settled by a live run once the driver can raise a dialog.

sources.note: aider 0.86.2 — the mid-turn TOOL-LESS dialogs: Coder.check_tokens (line 1396) -> confirm_ask("Try to proceed anyway?") at 1415, raised BEFORE the LLM call so no tool call exists or can release it; confirm_ask("Attempt to fix lint errors?") at 1604 and "Attempt to fix test errors?" at 1620, raised after the lint/test run has already finished. Also line 976 check_for_urls -> "Add URL to the chat?", cited only to record that it is a web-FETCH gate and therefore belongs to permission-gate-non-mutating-tool, not to this row. Anchors agent_supports: yes on trigger 4.

aider 0.86.2 first-use workspace trust prompts: confirm_ask("No git repo found, create one to track aider's changes (recommended)?") at line 122; confirm_ask("Add … to .gitignore (recommended)?") at 191; the analytics opt-in confirm_ask("Allow collection of anonymous analytics…?") at 649 (guarded by analytics.need_to_ask). Anchors agent_supports: yes on trigger 2 — and the driver's git-init + --no-gitignore suppress the first two.
line 93: confirm_ask("Login to OpenRouter or create a free account?") — the first-use provider trust/auth prompt, reached only when no API key is configured. Trigger 2.

EMPTY SCANS that anchor the two ABSENT triggers, cited so they are not re-litigated: `find … -name '*.py' -print0 | xargs -0 grep -in sandbox` returns zero matches across the installed 0.86.2 package (trigger 1 — no sandbox or network-egress confirmation exists); `xargs -0 grep -ln 'mcp\|MCP\|modelcontextprotocol'` returns zero FILES and `grep -in mcp args.py` is empty (trigger 3 — aider 0.86.2 ships no MCP client, so no server-driven elicitation is possible).

confirm_ask at line 807: the question is rendered ONLY via prompt_session.prompt/input (871-895) and never written to the history file. _tool_message (966-973) and tool_output (995-999) DO append blockquotes via append_chat_history (1117), which is how check_tokens' preamble reaches the transcript — the closest thing to an entry trace, and unmarked. confirm_ask("Try to proceed anyway?") passes no subject/group/allow_never, so neither post-answer write path fires and the release edge has no trace. `self.yes is True` short-circuits at 869-870, which is how --yes-always suppresses every dialog including the tool-less ones.

line 760: --yes-always is action="store_true", NOT argparse.BooleanOptionalAction (used for ~30 other aider flags) — so no --no-yes-always exists and the driver's hard-coded flag cannot be negated by appended aider_extra_args. Anchors driver_capability: gap:permission-approval.

ParseLineRaw emits only user_message/assistant_message/tool_result(Edit,Bash)/turn_done and drops non-error blockquotes with a comment naming "confirmation prompts". errorRE is `^>\s*\S*(?:Error|Exception)(?:[: ]|$)`, which the `> Your estimated chat context…` preamble does not match. IdleFlush synthesizes turn_done after aiderIdleTurnDoneAfter (1500ms) over a quiet transcript — the mechanism by which a blocked session is reported ready.

Source = FilesUnderCWD{.aider.chat.history.md, RawLineParser}; Permissions carries only ControlPermission + the `history` observe permission and no Hooks field — both hook-tier waiting signals are unreachable for aider.

stateRules lines 106-207: the five waiting-producing rules. SignalPermissionPrompt and SignalIdlePrompt are hook-fed; transcript_permission_prompt needs permission.requested/completed kinds; user_blocking_tool needs a user-blocking tool name; SignalOpenToolStalled needs an OPEN tool call — which THIS row's premise excludes by definition and aider cannot produce anyway. Line 437 carries the one path aider CAN reach (turn ended with question or cue -> waiting), the vacuous-pass hazard.
isUserBlockingToolName (lines 46-54) accepts only AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode/question/ask_user_question/exit_plan_mode/ask_user; aider's parser names only "Edit" and "Bash".

AIDER_ARGS=( --no-auto-commits --yes-always --no-gitignore ) is hard-coded and settings.aider_extra_args only appends; the driver also git-inits RUN_CWD before launch. DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn interrupt sleep" — no keys/approval step. Anchors driver_capability: gap:permission-approval and the rig-suppression caveat.
aider 0.86.2 options reference: --yes-always ("Always say yes to every confirmation") is the only blanket-approve flag and has no --no- counterpart; no MCP and no sandbox options are documented.

recipe.notes: FROZEN on the daemon axis (daemon_capability: incapable), and separately blocked on the driver axis (gap:permission-approval). Left applicable:false with no script — same shape as the opencode/tool-gate-permission-prompt sibling — because no step sequence could produce the assertion: (a) driver-interactive.sh hard-codes --yes-always and aider has no --no-yes-always (args.py:760 is action="store_true"), which suppresses EVERY confirm_ask including the tool-less ones; (b) there is no keys/approval step to answer one; and (c) even with both fixed, aider writes no dialog marker into .aider.chat.history.md and confirm_ask("Try to proceed anyway?") writes nothing at all on the answer, so neither edge this row asserts has a trace — IdleFlush would report the blocked session as `ready` after 1500ms of quiet, the inversion of the pinned-at-waiting failure the row's trailing idle exists to catch. WHAT THE RECIPE WOULD BE once (a) and (b) close: launch aider interactively WITHOUT --yes-always against a SMALL-context model (the trigger is context-window dependent); send a prompt large enough that Coder.check_tokens (base_coder.py:1396) finds the estimate over max_input_tokens and raises confirm_ask("Try to proceed anyway?") at line 1415 — a dialog raised BEFORE the LLM call, so no tool call exists, none is in flight, and none can complete to release it, which is exactly this row's premise; wait >=15s for the dialog to be visible; answer it with a literal `y` + Enter; wait_turn; then hold a >=15s trailing idle. A second usable trigger, if the context one proves hard to pin: run with --auto-lint and --lint-cmd set to a command that always fails, and let the post-edit confirm_ask("Attempt to fix lint errors?") (base_coder.py:1604) raise the dialog after the lint run has already finished. DO NOT substitute a tool-permission dialog — that is tool-gate-permission-prompt and permission-gate-non-mutating-tool, and this row forbids it.
preconditions: DRIVER CHANGE REQUIRED: drop the hard-coded --yes-always from AIDER_ARGS in replaydata/agents/aider/driver-interactive.sh (or make it settings-controlled). aider has no --no-yes-always to append (args.py:760 uses action="store_true"), so appended aider_extra_args cannot undo it. io.yes gates EVERY confirm_ask, so this suppresses the tool-less dialogs too.

DRIVER CHANGE REQUIRED: a step type that answers a TUI confirm_ask prompt (the scenario's `keys`). `send` types literal text + Enter and would mechanically answer y/n, but wait_turn counts `> Tokens:` lines and would need re-anchoring around a turn that pauses before any model call — check_tokens blocks BEFORE the LLM request, so no `> Tokens:` line will ever arrive while the dialog is open.

DAEMON CHANGE REQUIRED (the frozen axis): aider must write the dialog window into .aider.chat.history.md — an open marker at confirm_ask entry and a close at its return — or ship a hook channel. Without both edges no driver fix satisfies this row.

MODEL PINNING: the cleanest trigger (confirm_ask("Try to proceed anyway?")) fires only when the estimated context exceeds the model's max_input_tokens, read from litellm metadata. Pin a small-context model via IRRLICHT_AIDER_MODEL, or pad the chat with /read-only files, and re-probe the limit at record time rather than trusting a cached figure.

RE-PROBE AT RECORD TIME, do not trust this list: whether the alternate startup triggers can fire is host state, not aider state — main.py:122 needs a NON-git RUN_CWD (the driver git-inits it), main.py:191 needs --no-gitignore dropped, main.py:649 needs analytics.need_to_ask still true on this host, and onboarding.py:93 needs NO provider key configured.
aider CLI on PATH with a configured provider (aider needs paid API access; the recording environment has no aider auth today).
tmux available — the interactive driver keeps the REPL alive past turn end so the >=15s trailing idle is observable.
